83.en:
The House of Representatives consists of five hundred members: four hundred members elected on a constituency basis and one hundred members elected on a party-list basis.

The election of Members of the House of Representatives shall be by direct and secret ballot, using one ballot paper for each type of Member of the House of Representatives.

Where an office of a Member of the House of Representatives becomes vacant for any reason and an election has not yet been held, or the name of a replacement Member has not yet been announced, the House of Representatives shall consist of the existing Members.

Where, for any reason, the number of Members of the House of Representatives elected on a party-list basis is fewer than one hundred, the party-list Members of the House of Representatives shall consist of the existing Members.

86.en:
The determination of the number of Members of the House of Representatives to which each province is entitled, and the division of constituencies, shall follow this procedure:

(1) Divide the total number of inhabitants throughout the country, according to the population-registration figures published in the last year before the year of the election, by four hundred Members of the House of Representatives. The result shall be the number of inhabitants per Member.

(2) A province whose population is below the number of inhabitants per Member under (1) shall have one Member of the House of Representatives, with the whole province constituting one constituency.

(3) A province whose population exceeds the number of inhabitants per Member shall have one additional Member of the House of Representatives for each complete number of inhabitants equal to the number of inhabitants per Member.

(4) After the number of Members of the House of Representatives for each province has been determined under (2) and (3), if the total number of Members is still fewer than four hundred, the province with the largest remainder from the calculation under (3) shall receive one additional Member. Additional Members shall then be allocated in the same way to the provinces with the next-largest remainders, in descending order, until the total reaches four hundred.

(5) A province entitled to elect more than one Member of the House of Representatives shall be divided into as many constituencies as the number of Members to which it is entitled. The areas within each constituency must be contiguous, and the population of each constituency must be approximately equal.

91.en:
To calculate the proportion of candidates on each political party's list who are to be elected, combine the votes received by each political party throughout the country and calculate the number of candidates to be elected for each political party in direct proportion to those total votes. Candidates whose names appear on each political party's list shall be elected in accordance with the calculated vote-based allocation, in the numerical order in which their names appear on that party's list.

The rules, procedures and conditions governing applications for election as Members of the House of Representatives on a party-list basis, voting, vote counting, aggregation of votes, announcement of election results and other related matters shall be as prescribed by the Organic Act on Election of Members of the House of Representatives.
